00.summary: Foreword items are listed but not counted in either figure, because the chapters cover the same ground. Of the four original Foreword objectives, two are in effect: DEI and gender-term removal (EO 14151, EO 14168 and EO 14173 of January 2025, plus later agency rules) and international withdrawals (EO 14155, EO 14199 and a 2026-01-07 memorandum covering 66 organizations). The free-speech objective is underway under EO 14149 and FTC actions. For the pornography objective, two introduced bills (S. 1671, H.R. 3297) are the closest step, with no committee action found, and court challenges to the DEI orders remain pending.

01.summary: One of four objectives is in effect: since 2025-02-25 the White House, not the White House Correspondents' Association, selects the press pool, and litigation continues (Associated Press appeal argued 2025-11-24; a 14-day order of 2026-09-24 restored three outlets' hard passes). Three are underway: policy-council roles set by executive orders, Presidential Personnel Office clearance of Schedule C and Schedule G appointments, and a reported new White House Counsel contacts policy. No new Justice Department contacts policy was found as of 2026-10-08.

02.summary: Six of eight objectives are in effect. They rest on OMB's apportionment delegation (effective 2025-02-11), EO 14215 on OIRA review of independent agencies, CEQ's removal of its NEPA regulations (final rule effective 2026-01-08), EO 14168, EO 14148 and EO 14192 on regulatory review, and EO 14154 on social cost of carbon. NSC reorganization under NSPM-1 and a proposed amendment to the Fifth National Climate Assessment (noticed 2026-08-25) are underway, no life and family coordinator was found, and impoundment litigation continues.

03.summary: Five of nine objectives are in effect: Schedule Policy/Career (EO 14171; OPM rule effective 2026-03-09), limits on union bargaining (EO 14251, EO 14343), merit hiring (EO 14170), workforce controls (EO 14210; OPM reduction-in-force rule effective 2026-09-02) and Schedule G (EO 14317). Appraisal rules, pay and award changes, and function cuts are underway, and pay and retirement legislation was not enacted. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB is classed as diverged, because OPM rules moved several appeal categories to OPM. Lawsuits over several actions are pending.

04.summary: Three of eleven objectives are in effect: EO 14183 on transgender service (the certiorari petition in United States v. Talbott, No. 26-272, is pending), EO 14184 on reinstating members discharged over the COVID-19 vaccine (about 230 returned by July 2026, against roughly 8,700 eligible) and EO 14185 on DEI offices. Seven are underway, including acquisition reform (EO 14265), Golden Dome (EO 14186) and a general-officer cut announced 2026-09-30; the fleet stood at 291 ships against a 355 goal, and one officer still leads both NSA and Cyber Command.

05.summary: Five of twelve objectives are in effect: nationwide expedited removal (in effect since 2026-07-17, rehearing petition pending), detention and ICE funding (P.L. 119-21, P.L. 119-98), ended parole and TPS programs, 287(g) growth (2,510 agreements by 2026-09-15) and a final public charge rule (effective 2026-09-18, challenged in S.D.N.Y.). Five are underway, including wall funding and border asylum limits (a certiorari petition in RAICES v. Noem is pending), while replacing DHS and shifting disaster costs to states remain at the proposal stage.

06.summary: Eleven of nineteen tracked recommendations are classed as in effect, including all seven key objectives. Actions include EO 14163 suspending refugee entry, EO 14155 and EO 14199 with a 2026-01-07 memorandum covering 66 organizations, a State reorganization announced 2025-04-22 with layoff notices to more than 1,300 employees, and Proclamations 10949 and 10998 on entry, while NSPM-2 directs Iran sanctions (a June 2026 memorandum with Iran lapsed). Refugee ceilings go primarily to Afrikaners, and a 75-country immigrant visa pause was vacated on 2026-08-21. Among the twelve recommendations added in the fuller reading, the EO 14169 foreign aid pause and review, trade arrangements with the EU and the UK, and the return to the Geneva Consensus Declaration on 2025-01-24 are classed as in effect; seven are underway, including cartel terrorist designations under EO 14157 and Arctic icebreaker funding; no action was found on revoking Circular 175 authorities, and the United States has not recognized Somaliland.

07.summary: One of nineteen tracked recommendations is in effect: ODNI was restructured from 2025-08-20 (ODNI 2.0) with staff reductions; clearance revocations under EO 14152, leak policy changes and CIA workforce changes are underway. FISA Title VII, including Section 702, lapsed on 2026-06-12 after House votes failed, and collection was reported to continue under existing certifications. Classification reform and a bar on monitoring domestic disinformation remain at the proposal stage, and no action on EO 14086 was found. Of the twelve recommendations added in the fuller reading, none is in effect: five are partly underway (clearance reform, intelligence support for export control and investment review, the reported move of President's Daily Brief production to ODNI, post-quantum orders EO 14412 and EO 14413 of 2026-06-22, and commercial space integration under EO 14369), four are at the proposal stage, and no public action was found on a 60-day covert action review, a 48-hour cyber threat sharing rule or the composition rule for the National Intelligence Council.

08.summary: Two of six tracked recommendations are in effect: the Rescissions Act of 2025 (P.L. 119-28, signed 2025-07-24) cancelled about $1.1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and acting leadership was installed at USAGM, although a 2026-03-07 court ruling voided one official's acting-CEO actions. Two are underway: EO 14238 (2025-03-14) directed USAGM reduced to its statutory minimum while Congress enacted about $652.7 million for FY2026. The NCE-status objective remains a proposal, and no journalist safety measures were found.

09.summary: Seven of twenty tracked recommendations are in effect, among them foreign assistance placed under State with USAID wound down by 2025-07-01, aid reductions (P.L. 119-28), rules on gender, equity and abortion terms (effective 2026-02-26), an AGOA extension, the end of climate finance under EO 14162 and appointee review of awards under EO 14332. Ten are underway or proposed, including humanitarian aid, global health compacts, regional aid resets and branding. Two are classed as diverged (WHO withdrawal and the USAID staffing plan), and no change to section 653(a) reporting was found.

10.summary: Two of sixteen tracked recommendations are in effect: SNAP changes in P.L. 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) and the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines. Four are underway (forest management, the end of climate-smart commodity grants on 2025-04-14, rejection of the UN 2030 Agenda, biotechnology review changes) and four rest on introduced bills or early steps. Three are classed as diverged: P.L. 119-21 raised ARC/PLC reference prices and added trade promotion funding, and CRP signups continued. No action was found on moving nutrition programs to HHS, marketing orders or the Community Eligibility Provision.

11.summary: Six of twenty-two tracked recommendations are in effect: removal of the 2024 Title IX rule, borrowing caps and a new repayment plan, removal of disparate-impact provisions from Title VI rules, charter grants run without the 2022 requirements, a revised Civil Rights Data Collection and USDA's rescission of its school meals Title IX policy. Nine are underway, including program moves to other agencies and Section 117 enforcement under EO 14282. Five rest on proposals or bills, executive caps on research indirect costs were blocked in court, and no move to end negotiated rulemaking was found.

12.summary: Of the 21 tracked Department of Energy and related commission recommendations, 3 are in effect, including LNG export approvals, the end of DOE equity programs and the refusal of climate reparations, and 13 are underway, among them grid equipment security, cleanup and lab refocusing. Four have diverged, covering the Loan Programs Office, Yucca Mountain, FERC's transmission rule and reactor demonstrations, none is blocked, and no action was found for ending the Clean Energy Corps.

13.summary: Of 21 tracked EPA recommendations, 6 are in effect (implemented or completed), including the restored 2020 major-source reclassification rule and relaxed HFC technology transition limits. Another 13 are underway (in progress or proposed), such as regional haze, Good Neighbor, truck NOx, Risk Management Program and TSCA procedure rulemakings. One, the PFAS hazardous substance designation, is recorded as diverged, none is blocked, and no action was found on a stand-alone American Indian Office.

14.summary: Of the 24 tracked recommendations in the health and human services chapter, 6 are in effect (Hyde travel funding steps, fetal tissue research limits, conscience enforcement, EMTALA guidance rescission, HSA rules and CDC gender identity data), 13 are underway (including Medicaid work requirements, site-neutral payment, price transparency, 340B bills and teen pregnancy grants), 2 are blocked (vaccine safety transfer and Medicare Advantage audit rule) and 3 have diverged (CDC split, Head Start and drug price negotiation repeal).

15.summary: Of 15 tracked HUD recommendations, five are in effect, including the AFFH repeal, the end of PAVE appraisal policies, climate rollbacks, guidance withdrawals and reversals of prior diversity actions. Seven are underway, among them the noncitizen and work requirement proposals, Housing First changes, zoning and public housing provisions in a 2026 housing law, and budget-request devolution. None is blocked or diverged, and three show no action found: CFIUS membership, PD&R grant suspension and term-based FHA premiums.

16.summary: Of the 20 tracked Interior recommendations in this chapter, 8 are in effect (implemented), including oil and gas leasing, the 30 by 30 rescission, the Migratory Bird Treaty Act opinion, the Dalton corridor land order and congressional disapproval of recent BLM plans. Eleven are underway (7 in progress, 4 proposed), such as coal leasing, Endangered Species Act rules, the Boundary Waters and Chaco withdrawals and BLM headquarters, none are blocked or diverged, and 1, the BLM law enforcement chain of command, has no action found.

17.summary: Three of eleven objectives are in effect: alignment of DOJ litigation with the President's agenda (Attorney General memo of 2025-02-05, EO 14215 and Trump v. Slaughter of 2026-06-29), Civil Rights Division findings on race-conscious admissions, and review of consent decrees and FACE Act cases. Six are underway, including death penalty authorizations for 44 defendants (2026-04-24) and sanctuary jurisdiction suits that courts have dismissed. No Comstock Act enforcement announcement and no reassignment of election-related 18 U.S.C. 241 cases were found.

18.summary: Two of ten objectives are in effect: EO 11246 was revoked by EO 14173 (2025-01-21) with a Labor Department rescission rule effective 2026-10-26, though OFCCP still exists, and the NLRB and EEOC general counsels were replaced in January 2025. Three are underway, including disparate-impact limits under EO 14281, and four remain at the proposal stage, including an ERISA rule on ESG factors, for which no proposed rule was published. Capping H-2A and H-2B visas is classed as diverged, as DHS and DOL made 64,716 supplemental H-2B visas available.

19.summary: One of six objectives is in effect: NHTSA's final fuel economy rule (published 2026-09-30, effective 2026-11-30) and three Congressional Review Act resolutions nullifying California waivers (P.L. 119-15, 119-16, 119-17), with state challenges pending. Three are underway: air traffic control modernization funded at $12.5 billion in P.L. 119-21, drone and eVTOL programs under EO 14307, and automated vehicle rules. Converting discretionary grants to formulas and curbing transit subsidies remain at the proposal stage; a House committee bill, H.R. 8870, instead raises Mass Transit Account authorizations.

20.summary: One of six objectives is in effect: a VA final rule restoring the exclusion of abortion services (effective 2026-01-30) and a March 2025 rescission of the gender dysphoria care directive. Two are underway: claims processing (75.6 days in September 2026, from 141.5 on 2025-01-20) and the Oracle health record rollout (17 live sites). Codifying MISSION Act access standards (H.R. 740, reported by committee) and facility realignment remain at the proposal stage; the rating schedule revision is classed as blocked, as VA rescinded a related interim rule on 2026-02-27.

21.summary: One of seven objectives is in effect: NTIA's BEAD restructuring notice of 2025-06-06 ended the fiber preference, and all 56 final proposals were approved by 2026-08-25. Three are underway: NOAA staffing reductions (Congress kept the research office in FY2026 funding), a proposed census rule counting only citizens and lawful permanent residents for apportionment, and export control rules that tighten and loosen in turn. Two are blocked, as Congress funded EDA, MBDA and MEP in P.L. 119-74, and the space commerce objective (EO 14335) remains at the proposal stage.

22.summary: One of eight objectives is in effect: Treasury and FinCEN exempted domestic companies from Corporate Transparency Act reporting (final rule effective 2026-08-14), though the statute stands. Four are underway: P.L. 119-21 phased out many IRA credits and made the estate tax exemption permanent, IRS management changes, outbound investment rules in the FY2026 NDAA, and a side-by-side OECD agreement (2026-01-05). P.L. 119-21 kept seven individual rates (classed as diverged); ending the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac conservatorships and repealing Dodd-Frank Titles I, II and VIII remain at the proposal stage.

23.summary: The chapter presents two opposing positions. Reauthorizing the Export-Import Bank is underway: it operates with a three-member Board (President and Chair confirmed 2025-09-18), approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, and has a charter running to 2026-12-31, with S. 3772 and a House draft pending and no markup reported. Abolishing the Bank is classed as diverged, since no step toward abolition was found and the FY2027 request raises EXIM's program budget to $200 million.

24.summary: One of four objectives is in effect: an executive order of 2025-01-23 bars executive-agency work on a central bank digital currency, followed by a statutory bar in P.L. 119-101 (dated 2026-07-11, expiring 2030-12-31). Fed regulation changes are underway, including withdrawal of the 2023 climate risk principles (notice 2025-11-18). A House committee reported H.R. 5396, removing the employment goal, on 2026-06-24 with no floor vote, while the Fed ended balance sheet reduction on 2025-12-01 and began Treasury bill purchases (classed as diverged from shrinking it).

25.summary: One of five objectives is in effect: SBA fraud cleanup of COVID-era PPP and EIDL loans (over 560,000 borrowers referred to Treasury on 2026-04-24; 870,000 suspensions announced 2026-09-14). Two are underway: removal of the religious-entity exclusion for disaster loans (announced 2025-07-14) and SBIR and STTR continuation through 2031-09-30 (P.L. 119-83). Strengthening the Office of Advocacy is at the proposal stage, and no action ending SBA direct lending was found; the FY2027 request cuts disaster loan funding to $143 million.

26.summary: One of seven objectives is in effect: de minimis treatment ended for China (EO 14256, effective 2025-05-02) and for all countries (EO 14324, effective 2025-08-29). Three are underway: executive trade arrangements without renewed Trade Promotion Authority, outbound investment rules in the FY2026 NDAA, and a temporary Jones Act waiver to 2026-11-15. Reciprocal tariff authority is blocked after Learning Resources v. Trump (2026-02-20, IEEPA does not authorize tariffs); China decoupling and repeal of Section 232, 201 and 301 tariffs are classed as diverged, since those tariffs were kept.

27.summary: None of five objectives is in effect. Three are underway: the SEC proposed rescinding its climate disclosure rules on 2026-05-29 (no final rescission), proposed capital formation changes in May 2026, and issued a joint SEC and CFTC crypto interpretation on 2026-03-23, followed by a proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. Abolishing the CFPB is blocked (the Bureau still exists and an injunction against mass layoffs remains), as is abolishing the PCAOB and FINRA (the Senate parliamentarian ruled the PCAOB provision out of the 2025 reconciliation law).

28.summary: None of six objectives is in effect. Four are underway: FCC Covered List additions of foreign-produced drones (2025-12-22), spectrum auctions required by P.L. 119-21 (Auction 115 proposed for 2027-04-27), satellite and wireline permitting actions, and an order repealing the 39 percent national television ownership cap (voted 2026-08-06, not yet published). The TikTok app was not banned (a U.S. joint venture closed 2026-01-22), platform contributions to the Universal Service Fund are proposed in two bills with no committee action, and no FCC action on Section 230 was found.

29.summary: None of three objectives is in effect. The coordination objective is underway through a court ruling: on 2026-06-30 the Supreme Court held in NRSC v. FEC, 6 to 3, that limits on party coordinated expenditures violate the First Amendment, and no statute raising contribution limits was found. The FEC has lacked a quorum since 2025-05-01, with two nominees named 2026-02-11 unconfirmed, and no directive limiting DOJ prosecution of FECA violations or having DOJ defend the FEC was found.

30.summary: One of four objectives is complete: Trump v. Slaughter (decided 2026-06-29, 6 to 3) held FTC commissioners removable at will and overruled Humphrey's Executor, after the President removed two commissioners on 2025-03-18. Three are underway through individual actions: consent orders barring advertising agencies from coordinating on political or ideological viewpoints, enforcement of the amended COPPA Rule with an AI chatbot inquiry, and non-price harm analysis in merger orders. No FTC task force on ESG or DEI collusion was found.

limits: The headline counts every recommendation tracked so far, 373 today, not every recommendation in the roughly 900-page document. The record began as key objectives from all 30 chapters and is being extended chapter by chapter by reading each chapter in full, so chapters read in full contribute more recommendations than the rest and the figure will move as more are added. Recommendations added in the fuller reading have had one independent review and no red-team pass yet. Foreword items are listed but not counted, because the chapters cover the same ground.
Research and review are done by AI models. Every claim links to its source so that a person can check it, and each objective carries a confidence rating. Errors are possible; corrections are welcome.

Research ran in five passes under a fixed web search budget: a first pass on 2026-10-07, a validation pass on the weakest and in-effect objectives, an in-depth pass that re-researched weak records and added objectives in every chapter, a targeted pass on 2026-10-08 on every objective still rated low confidence, and a primary-source pass the same day that located the deciding official document for records previously rated on secondary sources. Objectives rated medium or low confidence still rest on limited searching, and developments from mid-2026 onward are the most likely to be missing.
A status of "No action found" means the research found none. It is weaker evidence than a documented action, and the reviewer caps its confidence accordingly.
Objectives are not independent. One law, order, or court ruling can count toward several objectives, so the headline share is not a count of separate government actions.
Progress percentages come from a fixed rubric and the average is unweighted. Objectives differ greatly in importance, so the average is a rough gauge only.
Status describes alignment between actions and the document. Officials have said the administration does not follow the document, and many actions have other origins.
Estimated timeframes are inferences from the legal route each objective needs. They are not predictions from any official schedule.

significance.note: Recomputed on 2026-10-11 for the single headline set of 257 counted recommendations. The page computes the weighted share live from the scores on each record. Rater agreement figures are from the original scoring of 219 objectives; the bootstrap range has not been recomputed.

trackers.name: Project 2025 Tracker (project2025.observer)
trackers.note: a community tracker organized by agency with three statuses (completed, in progress, not started); it listed 321 objectives with 141 completed and 70 in progress when read on 2026-10-08. It runs advertising and donation links.

trackers.name: Center for Progressive Reform and Governing for Impact executive action tracker
trackers.note: an advocacy-organization tracker; it reported 283 of 532 domestic executive actions initiated or completed as of its February 2026 update.

update_note: The record is refreshed every Tuesday and Thursday morning (Pacific time). Each run searches official sources and the press for developments on every tracked objective, updates status and evidence, sends changed objectives to an independent review, and logs the changes under Changes. Daily runs are planned once the beta settles. Requests made under Requirements are picked up by the next run.
